recommendations.current: The shape recurs across four other well-cited audits: Ferrari Dacrema et al. diagnose recommender-system progress as an artifact of "(i) weak baselines; (ii) establishment of weak methods as new baselines; and (iii) difficulties in comparing or reproducing results across papers," then re-run with tuned baselines and find six of seven neural methods lose to classical algorithms [3]; Musgrave et al. rebuild the deep-metric-learning protocol and find "the actual improvements over time have been marginal at best" [4]; Lucic et al. show that for generative adversarial networks "most models can reach similar scores with enough hyperparameter optimization and random restarts" [21]; and Agarwal et al. supply the statistical-methodology version, a three-part taxonomy of evaluation confounds with demonstrated ranking reversals [22]. - **Ferrari Dacrema et al.** diagnose recommender-system progress as an artifact of "(i) weak baselines; (ii) establishment of weak methods as new baselines; and (iii) difficulties in comparing or reproducing results across papers," then re-run with tuned baselines and find six of seven neural methods lose to classical algorithms [3].
- **Musgrave et al.** rebuild the deep-metric-learning protocol and find "the actual improvements over time have been marginal at best" [4].

- **Agarwal et al.** supply the statistical-methodology version, a three-part taxonomy of evaluation confounds with demonstrated ranking reversals [22].
